clue.text: Cheer old troopers during dance

indicators.note: the old troopers sit during, that is in the middle of, the dance word

parts.note: a hay is an old country dance
OR, other ranks, the ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Veteran soldiers whoop it up in the middle of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooray is a shout of joy, the same as a cheer from a crowd.

clue.text: Harry girl admitting paper's misleading remark

indicators.note: the pair of names let in, so contain, the paper letters

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Harry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
Ruth is a girl's name
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Harry's girlfriend owns up that the newspaper's claim was misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-truth tells only part of the facts so as to deceive, a misleading statement.

clue.text: Test covers part of town bypass perhaps

indicators.note: the test word covers, so wraps round, the part

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam, a test
a bit is a part of something

explanation.surface: An exam covering one part of town planning.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital road circles a town or city; a ring-road bypass is an example.

clue.text: Head of army strips standing up in bed?

indicators.note: the head of army is its first letter
in a down clue standing up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to peel is to strip off clothing or skin

explanation.surface: An army chief undresses and is up, or is he in bed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' reverses PEELS in this down entry to SLEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in bed is usually sleeping, so asleep is a fair example.

clue.text: Sort of clock face seen crossing grand city centre

indicators.note: the face word stretches across, so it goes round, the other letters

parts.note: the dial is the face of a clock or meter
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

indicators.note: the centre of the word city is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A clock face is spotted spanning the heart of a great city.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital clock shows the time in numerals rather than with hands on a face.

clue.text: Time-consuming end of Oxford dictionary was far from sound

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of Oxford
the dictionary eats up, contains, the time letter

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: Consulting the Oxford dictionary takes up time, and something about it was unsound.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote once meant to be feeble-minded with age, so doted means was mentally unsound.

clue.text: One female in fast car stole parcel for birthday?

indicators.note: one and the female letter go in the fast car letters

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a fast touring car
I is the Roman numeral for one
a wrap is a shawl or stole

explanation.surface: A woman in a sports car wears a stole as a birthday gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To giftwrap is to wrap a present in decorative paper, so to parcel up a birthday gift.

clue.text: Given tribute when carried outside

indicators.note: the carried word sits outside, wrapping round, the word for when

parts.note: to tote is to carry
as can mean when, as in as I arrived

explanation.surface: Someone was honoured while being carried out on shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: To be toasted is to be honoured with raised glasses, a tribute paid by drinkers.

clue.text: End up defending conservative doctor once

indicators.note: the turned word defends, so surrounds, the conservative letter
in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a heel is an end, as the heel of a loaf

explanation.surface: A conservative doctor finishes up on the defensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses HEEL to LEEH, which holds C. Leech was an old word for a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech was an old word for a physician, from doctors' use of bloodsucking leeches.

clue.text: European sailor clutching second leading light?

indicators.note: the European and sailor words together clutch, holding between them, the second letter

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A Polish sailor holds on briefly to a guiding figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole star guides navigators north, literally a light that leads the way.

clue.text: Tag lines Lincoln introduced

indicators.note: Lincoln is brought in between the two line letters

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL
Abe is the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A tag line coined by President Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag attached to something to identify it is a label; both nouns name the same thing.

clue.text: Square, where stone comes from?

definitions.meaning: square in the sense of old-fashioned, behind the times
the stone of a date comes out of the date fruit

explanation.surface: A quarry question: where do stones for a town square come from?
explanation.walkthrough: The stone is the seed of a date palm's fruit, which is taken out of the date.
explanation.definitionFit: A square person is conventional and unfashionable, as are old-fashioned, obsolete things.

clue.text: Legal document fool took across river

parts.note: a tit is a fool in British slang

indicators.note: the word for took lies across the river, so the river sits inside it

parts.note: led as in took someone somewhere
the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A foolish person escorting a document over the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal paper that proves who owns a property.

clue.text: Enchanting woman accompanying boxing clubs

indicators.note: the accompanying word boxes in, that is encloses, the clubs letter

parts.note: with means accompanying, together alongside
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A charming woman accompanying a crowd at a boxing club.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch casts enchantments, so a woman who enchants by spells is a witch.

clue.text: Nasty bloke, putting head back, crossing line

indicators.note: the rearranged bloke word goes across the line letter, holding it inside
the head, first letter, of the bloke word is moved back one place

parts.note: guy is a casual word for a man, a bloke

explanation.surface: An unpleasant man throws his head back and steps over a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting head back' moves G of GUY back to give UGY; 'crossing' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean unpleasant or threatening, as in an ugly mood, so it is a synonym of nasty.

clue.text: It helps to climb, walk and run

parts.note: to step is to walk
a ladder is a run in tights or stockings, the British term

explanation.surface: Climbing is aided by walking and running.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder in British usage is a run in stockings or tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepladder is a folding ladder used to reach heights, so it is a climbing aid.

clue.text: Pick fruit etcetera regularly brought in

indicators.note: the picked letters are brought into the fruit word

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of etcetera, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Choose fruit and other things on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: A plectrum is the pick a guitarist uses to pluck strings.

clue.text: Unoriginal confused daydream about theatre's closure

indicators.note: the muddled letters go about, so round, the last letter
confused means the letters are muddled into a new order
the closure of theatre is its final letter

explanation.surface: A muddled daydream about a theatre closing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges DAYDREAM to READYMAD, and 'about' puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ready-made is bought off the shelf, not made specially, so it is unoriginal.

clue.text: American loudly leaving in a rage, attracting much interest

indicators.note: the loudly letter is leaving, so taken out of, the rage word

parts.note: furious means in a rage
F is forte, the musical direction for loudly

explanation.surface: An American storms out furiously, drawing lots of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' deletes F from FURIOUS. 'much interest' means high interest charged on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurious lending charges extortionate interest rates, which is what usury means.

clue.text: Get new tights here?

indicators.note: new tells us to make the letters into something fresh, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A suggestion of where to shop for fresh hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TIGHTS HERE; the whole clue also says where you would buy tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A town's high street is its main shopping road, where clothes such as tights are sold.

clue.text: Spot good story involving people in a house

indicators.note: the story word involves, so encloses, the people

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib
MPs are Members of Parliament, who sit in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A good tale about people living in a house is a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to catch sight of, as is to glimpse something briefly.

clue.text: Capital forfeits one seat

indicators.note: the capital gives up the letter standing for one

parts.note: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A capital city loses a seat, perhaps in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered piece of furniture for sitting, a long seat.

clue.text: Scrap old leaders in Daily Mail during depression

indicators.note: the picked letters come during, so in the middle of, the depression

parts.note: a dent is a hollow, a depression

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Old newspaper editorials thrown out in a gloomy period.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover piece, a scrap of fabric or other material.

clue.text: Feel bad securing dry nick

indicators.note: the rearranged letters secure, so hold inside, the dry letters
bad means the letters have gone wrong and need rearranging

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry, not drinking

explanation.surface: A man feels awful at getting a dry cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' makes FELE, which 'securing' wraps round the dry letters. 'Nick' is the British sense of condition, not a cut or theft.
explanation.definitionFit: In good nick and in fine fettle are both British idioms for being in good condition.

clue.text: Pipe what's brought on board by waiter finally?

parts.note: brie is a cheese served on a cheeseboard

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of waiter

explanation.surface: A waiter carries something onto a ship, which turns out to be a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A brier pipe is a tobacco pipe carved from the root of the briar heath, often just called a brier.

clue.text: Joy swept up contents of fossil bed

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top
contents of means the letters are inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Delight at sweeping up the remains of a fossil seam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of' takes SSILB from 'fossil bed' and 'swept up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bliss is perfect happiness, a near synonym of great joy.

clue.text: Modern coffee bar daughter opens

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: the daughter letter opens up the pair of words by going inside them

parts.note: a ray, a beam or bar of light

explanation.surface: A daughter opens a coffee bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Latter-day means belonging to recent times, a present-day version, hence modern.

clue.text: Flower of Wolves cut

indicators.note: cut means the word's tail is chopped off

parts.note: lupine means of or like wolves

explanation.surface: A flower belonging to Wolves, the football club, has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club, in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant grown for its tall spikes of colourful blooms.

clue.text: The writer's cue initially unthinkingly unscripted

parts.note: the writer is I, so the writer's, or the writer is, gives I'M
a prompt is a cue given to an actor

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of unthinkingly

explanation.surface: An actor admits speaking his cue without thinking, off-script.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu speech is improvised, done without preparation or a script.

clue.text: Letter or article accompanying grateful comment

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A letter, or an article, accompanied by a word of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Child recalled no small animals

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: A child remembered having no little animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a child of one's spouse from a previous relationship.

clue.text: Pagan ignores one kind

indicators.note: the pagan word ignores, that is leaves out, the letter for one

parts.note: a gentile is a heathen or pagan in old usage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A heathen snubs someone kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle person is mild and tender, much the same as a kind one.
